$comment: NEW 2026-09-04, and it exists because governance_reporter's first run made a
confident FALSE claim without it.
THE FAILURE: asked which standards each CDE carries, the agent read the CDE
list, found `sources` empty on every element, and reported 'no standard is
formally attached to any CDE'. That is wrong — Position As-of Date visibly
carries four BCBS 239 standards in CDE Manager. Standards attach through
`fields`, NOT `sources`; a CDE's `sources` is something else entirely. The
agent had no way to see `fields`, so it answered from the nearest field that
looked plausible.
Same shape as the standards list/detail split: a LIST is a summary, and an
agent asked to reason about what a list does not carry will reason from what
it does. The fix is the detail read, not a sterner instruction.
This also supplies PDE relationships. Without it the reporter cannot tell a
`control_point` from a `suggested` column, and control-point coverage is half
the data-quality story — a column that is merely suggested cannot carry a
monitor at all.
UNVERIFIED: this path is the documented get-one sibling of the CDE list and
create endpoints, both proven. It has not been called. Test it through
`Test tool` first — it declares one scalar, so unlike Create Critical Data
Element it can be.
name: Fetch Critical Data Element Detail
description: Read one Critical Data Element in full, by its integer id — including the overlay standards attached to it and its physical data elements with the relationship of each (control_point, related or suggested). Use this whenever you need to know what actually governs an element or which columns it is bound to: the CDE list is a summary and carries neither. Note that attached standards appear under 'fields', not under 'sources' — a CDE's sources field is unrelated to its standards, and reading it instead will tell you an element is ungoverned when it is not.

cde_id.description: The element's integer id, as returned by List Critical Data Elements. Not its UUID key.
